This study examines a partnership between a content provider (CP) and network service operator (OSP), exploring how to incentivize the CP to utilize high-traffic routes by proposing a profit-sharing contract framework that considers investment in the CP side. Specifically, the CP decides whether to deploy edge caching or prioritize caching popular titles, while the network operator can choose to upgrade infrastructure to higher quality standards or maintain current capabilities. The text analyzes the optimal profit allocation under these four distinct scenarios: when the CP invests in full caching with the OSP status quo, when the CP invests in full caching with the OSP status unchanged, when the CP invests in full caching with the OSP status unchanged (repeated context implies distinct comparisons here), and when the CP invests in full caching with the OSP status unchanged (rephrased based on standard game theory inputs to avoid contradiction: CP full caching/OSP status, CP full caching/OSP status, CP popular titles only/OSP status, CP popular titles only/OSP status). Using backward induction to solve this sequential game, the research derives conditions for market adoption of new services within each contract type and presents numerical results highlighting how CP market share impacts the optimal choice of profit allocation contracts.

We present a bi-directional association: starting from a finite collection of operators on a finite-dimensional vector space, one can either total the space of states into a 2-categorical framework or reconstruct the original operator set by starting with a collection of "states" organized as a hom-monoidal category. This paper explores this equivalence with a focus on the domain theory of ordered sets and provides examples demonstrating that the constructed "states" are both mathematically rigorous and physically significant.

$\alpha$-attractor models have recently gained prominence in the realm of inflationary cosmology due to their promising theoretical advantages and the feasibility of obtaining large expansion factors through simple constructions. This review summarizes the model class, analyzes various specific realizations, and discusses predicted consequences for post-inflationary physics, including constraints from primordial gravitational waves and the resulting implications for the universe's reheating temperature and reheating temperature.

The results provide a characterization of measured laminations at the boundary of quasi-Fuchsian surfaces that are near the Fuchsian locus through measured geodesic laminations on the Riemann surface. This is achieved by exploiting a newly established one-to-one correspondence between these laminans on the boundary of the manifold and those on the surface. To achieve this, the work extends the dynamical systems framework—encompassing geodesic flows, measured foliations, and laminations—at the Kleinian group level from individual quasi-Fuchsian cases to broader families of such groups.

This study investigates the allocation of risk returns across cross-sections of portfolios, similar to how Fama (1970) examined individual asset return allocation. The analysis begins with a simple model featuring a single investor and expands to scenarios with multiple investors, subsequently deriving an alternative expression for the cross-sectional allocation of return risk that relies exclusively on risk aversion and the return covariance matrix. This derived framework is then used to re-examine Fama's (1970) results and is applied to reassess the findings of Fama and French (2018) regarding the puzzle of factor risks versus premiums.

Existing methods for detecting abnormal heart sounds typically depend on manual feature extraction and rule-based methodologies. In contrast, this work introduces a rule-free approach utilizing self-parsing CNNs to classify the three primary categories of heart sounds. After training these networks on a dataset of 1,022 recordings, the system achieved an accuracy of 96.67%. Notably, con-vNet networks employing smaller filters outperformed larger filter configurations and matched the results of feature-engineered models. Additionally, this research investigates how different noise levels and types affect classification outcomes, revealing that Gaussian mixture model (GMM)-based denoising effectively enhanced accuracy. The results also highlight that CNN architectures utilizing smaller filters offer greater robustness when dealing with distorted inputs.

In this letter, we conduct a comprehensive analysis of nuclear and atomic effects within the $^{133}$Cs parity-violating system to evaluate limits on nuclear force helicity dependences. We demonstrate that near cancellation between the valence electron spin-inducing polarization of the core and the core's inherent negative polarization significantly reduces sensitivity to such forces, resulting in tighter constraints on them.

In the context of K-theory, topological twists on the torus are defined as pairs consisting of a line bundle and a non-trivial automorphism of this bundle's restriction to the torus' boundary. These twist configurations fall into classes categorized by the respective automorphism type. For a given class, the set of possible twists forms a discrete set isomorphic to the lattice dual under a specific metric induced by the twist. We provide an explicit calculation for this isomorphism. Additionally, we classify the classes themselves by their type: for point groups $G_{2,4,6}$—corresponding to wallpaper groups possessing a $p^g$-orbit within the torus—a class is uniquely specified by its relation to the lattice dual under a $G_{2}$ action; for groups $G'_{2}, {4'}$, and $G'_{6}$, or the wall paper group $G'_{6}$, only a single class exists, whereas for the group $G'_{4.1}$, two classes are present. Finally, we note that for a class containing a $p^g$-orbit, there is a non-trivial relation connecting the set of twists to the set of connections (or $U(1)$ gauge fields) within the torus.

This study analyzes endogenous community formation and cooperative climate responses within an overlapping generations framework. It establishes that multiple equilibria, including distinct communities, invariably exist. When individuals possess sufficient knowledge regarding their birth location, the resulting partition into communities may prevent Pareto-impossible outcomes. However, in scenarios characterized by high uncertainty about these origins, such division hampers cooperation, heightens saving rates, accelerates capital accumulation, and drives down per capita growth rates, ultimately worsening environmental degradation. These insights remain robust against variations in production techniques, whether they rely on extensive or intensive forms. Beyond these core contributions, the model offers additional potential for research regarding the effects of information on economic outcomes, differentiating returns on capital based on young versus old agents, examining inter-temporal price dynamics, and exploring inter-temporal inter-temporal allocations.

We introduce novel series operators associated with fractional-order Toeplitz matrices defined on discrete $H^2$ spaces (analytic on the unit disk and boundary). Our initial focus examines the invertibility of these matrices when the symbols are monomials of arbitrary order. Subsequently, we establish boundedness conditions for these operators in general cases and symbolically compute their matrix representations. Finally, our analysis extends to operators acting within the space of analytic polynomials of specific degrees.

This study involves Second-Price Auctions (SPAs) to conduct an experiment on trustworthiness. In this setup, a "seller" sets the auction's reserve price, while buyers submit bids. The final outcome is determined by the higher of these two figures: the highest bid or the preset reserve price. Slightly deviating from standard SPA rules allows us to investigate buyer behavior reserve prices set at various levels by high- and low-ability sellers. Our findings indicate that buyers trust reserve prices from low-ability sellers more than those from high-ability ones. Furthermore, when buyers submit bids exceeding their private valuations in response to a non-zero reserve price from a high-ability seller, this suggests a perceived lack of trust. Interestingly, this experiment demonstrates that buyer bids remain strictly below their private valuations even when facing prices from low-ability sellers, implying a stronger trust there. Lastly, our results show that buyer bids decline as the spread between high- and low-ability levels increases.

Although $f(Q)$-gravitational theory offers a $f(R)$-analogue within a totally antisymmetric symmetric metric by linearizing the pseudo-pseudotensor density of the Riemann curvature, its dynamical properties under linearly rotating anisotropic local anisotropy Bianchi-I conditions have not been adequately explored. In the current investigation, we examine the evolution of a locally rotated anisotropic Bianchi-I universe within $f(Q)$ gravity. The acceleration behavior is studied using an appropriate method. Our results demonstrate that the scale factor exhibits a power law in relation to time, and under specific constraints, the cosmological model transitions from a decelerated to an accelerated phase. Additionally, a stability inquiry into the model's behavior is conducted using an appropriate method.

This work establishes an explicit relationship between the coordinate ring of a regular nilpotent Hessenberg variety and an ideal generated by elementary symmetric functions and Geometric Vertex Decompositions (GV-decompositions) on this polynomial ring. By leveraging the Geometric Gale Dual Polyhedral Family framework and employing a coordinate system where the Hessenberg variety sits at a vertex of its ambient space, the authors provide a combinatorial description ofGV-decompositions in terms of Young Tableaux. Finally, these findings are connected to initial ideals of invariants of binary forms of degree n+1.

Recent theoretical efforts to explain the $\text{BCS}$ and $\text{K}_\text{B}$ anomalies, which stem from the electroweak baryon and lepton flavor anomalies observed in proton-proton collisions at the LHC, have proposed new magnetic resonance production mechanisms for charged resonances ($X^+$ and $Y^-$) within flavor-conserving frameworks at tree level involving flavor-changing neutral bosons ($Z'$). Leveraging these non-universal flavor-changing interactions, we demonstrate that charged resonance pairs can be effectively modeled as constituent quark-antiquark bound states ($X^+ = \bar{u}c$, $Y^- = d,s,t$). Furthermore, we show that quark compositeness itself provides a robust description of the flavor-changing neutral currents facilitating the generation of $X^+$ and $Y^-$, while simultaneously addressing the associated $K_B$ anomalies in proton-proton lepton production via decays of the charged di-boson states. Consequently, quark compositeness emerges as a unified solution for the proton-proton resonance production and the concurrent flavor-changing neutral currents, as well as explaining the flavor-changing neutral currents in the context of the current LHC data.

Knowledge-seeing queries—those focused on acquiring novel insights, enhancing understanding, or mastering new abilities—are infrequent in current question-asking models, which predominantly prioritize fact retrieval. To address this, we introduce PQA, an innovative dataset comprising over 10,000 search-seeking queries paired with detailed answer explanations grounded in the full texts of research papers. The dataset's construction involved two key steps: first, queries were crafted by experts to elucidate specific research findings using specialized literature as a reference; second, queries were augmented with contextual background to mitigate excessive reliance on external information. To address these characteristics, we proposed "Multi-Step ReInforcement learning with Document Anchors" (Multi-Step ReI), a fresh architecture for knowledge-inquiry tasks that integrates chain reasoning with document-grounded training. Our experiments demonstrate that this approach substantially outperforms prior methods paired with extensive linguistic resources, achieving over a 10% boost in EM scores. Furthermore, interactions with the model reveal its capacity to generate useful, search-directed responses.

Recent research indicates that the standard short-range $\nu_\mu \to \bar{\nu}_\mu$ regeneration, initially proposed to resolve the post-shock flavor deficit in three-dimensional supernova simulations, may actually originate within the convective core rather than the shock front alone. This revised understanding highlights that such regeneration is essential for maintaining the high-lepton number asymmetry required to sustain the long-standing short-time scale fast instabilities associated with three-dimensional neutrino transport. Furthermore, these instances suggest that the standard long-time scale anti-neutrino-driven instability can persist in three-dimensional supernova simulations. Ultimately, the confluence of these complementary instabilities, especially when mediated by shock turbulence, presents a viable route to generate long-wavelength perturbations capable of expanding the core convection zone, thereby amplifying the signatures of fast instabilities within observed three-dimensional core-collapse events.

Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) remains a prevalent psychiatric condition among children, yet its lack of definitive biomarkers hinders accurate clinical diagnosis. Previous research has indicated that rs-fMRI signals from specific neural regions in ADHD patients differ significantly from those of typically developing (TD) individuals. Despite this finding, standard machine learning approaches often fail to reliably distinguish between ADHD and TD groups. This study introduces a deep learning framework to identify the specific brain regions crucial for distinguishing ADHD patients from TD controls. The proposed system consists of two main modules: a multi-task network designed to locate significant regions for classification, followed by a second multi-task network that reconstructs these essential regions to generate observations for a final classifier. Testing on the ADNI2000 dataset revealed that, similar to prior studies, the default mode network (DMN) exhibited the most pronounced classification differences between the two groups. The three-stage deep learning approach achieved an accuracy of 67.3% in distinguishing the populations.

This research introduces a discrete-time Disease outbreak SISi model tailored for scenarios involving seasonal variations or periodic interventions; unlike continuous-time outbreak models, this discrete-time framework ensures that transmission and recovery rates remain finite and realistic by explicitly accounting for competing risks during each time step, specifically that an individual cannot simultaneously infect others, recover, or remain susceptible within the same interval. Furthermore, the basic reproduction number $R_0$ is defined to reflect the effectiveness of interventions or the intensity of seasonality. Finally, the study analyzes the long-term dynamics regarding the global asymptotic stability of disease-free and endemic equilibrium points and numerically compares continuous and discrete time outcomes to outline future research trajectories.

In recent years, the volume of text generated within social media platforms has surged dramatically. This expansion presents substantial challenges for automated systems tasked with comprehending context, specifically regarding the identification of acronyms and the resolution of domain-specific jargon. Addressing this gap, we introduce MadDog, a web-based platform dedicated to semantic acronym identification and disambiguation. During its development, we introduced the MadDogg dataset, a carefully curated collection extracted from Twitter messages containing over 10,000 annotated acronyms across various contexts. Furthermore, we evaluated multiple machine learning approaches to determine their efficacy in this domain.

This research introduces and analyzes an innovative mechanism for directional heat flow control within non-equilibrium quantum systems, achieved solely through the interference patterns of electronic states at a quantum Hall bar junction. By fine-tulating the electronic wave function interference at a quantum point contact connecting two bars, we establish an asymmetric correlation between electron fluctuations and energy. This asymmetry, rather than any physical structural imbalance, enables both thermal switching and rectification. Specifically, while the lower Fermi energy result in no net current due to identical current fluctuations, raising this energy induces thermoelectric power generation via an electron-selective backscattering process driven by interference, while also facilitating heat rectification at constant energy levels by an inter-electron and intra-electron correlation effect. This phenomenon offers promising avenues for compact devices operating under quantum coherence.

Encoding English text directly onto DNA necessitates expanding the character set beyond standard ASCII (which is limited to 256 symbols) by utilizing Hexadecimal (with 168 possible combinations. To maintain data integrity, we introduce three robust parity-check algorithms capable of identifying and correcting errors. Furthermore, we represent file hierarchies via structural checks to ensure consistency. Together, these approaches allow for highly compact storage—reducing the total number of encoded files while bolstering the storage system's overall reliability.

Nodal lines serve as two-dimensional representations of the momentum-space expression for a topological invariant characterized by a quantized chirp. Driven by robust mechanisms, these lines remain protected against perturbations. We examine two distinct forms of topological constant control related to topological charge or chirp: the first arises as a bulk property inherent to the material's constitution, whereas the second results from dynamic interactions between two or more components within heterostructures. Furthermore, the paper outlines pioneering experimental manifestations in condensed matter physics, quantum magnetism, and acoustics, as well as innovations in nanophotonics—the latter notably leveraging guided electronic and magnetic resonant interactions within magnetic resonance resonator (MRR) configurations to generate and utilize lines of nodal points in physical systems.

Waves initiated by a pacemaker within an excitable medium are defined as traveling loops characterized by wavefronts moving outward in both directions. This study presents an analytical framework to determine the constant propagation velocities of such loops by calculating the speeds of singular waves traveling in each direction and averaging the result. Utilizing the singular wave approximation previously established by Jackson and Beene for one-dimensional forward propagation, we separately apply this method to derive the velocities for both inward and outward moving waves, subsequently finding their arithmetic mean. To validate this approach, comparisons with actual velocities of pacemaker waves in two- and three-dimensional media reveal relative errors of approximately 1% or less. Consequently, the findings suggest that determining loop speeds via the approximation of individual component singular waves is highly precise. This simplicity and accuracy make the proposed method a valuable tool for efficiently estimating loop velocities in computational models of excitable media.

Deep learning and AI have witnessed unprecedented growth in recent years, driven by significant advancements and increased adoption across numerous industries. As models become more intricate and scale up, they demand extensive computational resources, financial backing, data availability, storage capacity, and consistent maintenance. Consequently, this paper examines these essential technical pillars—specifically data storage, cloud infrastructure, and AI pipelines—to highlight the increasing requirements for human and monetary investment. By analyzing these components, the work aims to help stakeholders assess their existing capabilities against project needs and make informed decisions regarding future AI maintenance and data management strategies.

ICD-10 codes categorize diseases and diagnoses, and analyzing them offers valuable insights into public health, clinical, and scientific research. However, extracting these codes from electronic health records (EHR) is challenging and labor-intensive, especially since unstructured text requires specialist medical coders. Consequently, researchers have developed numerous Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools to classify ICD-10 codes from patient notes. While initial studies relied on handcrafted rules, subsequent approaches adopted supervised machine learning using features like word embeddings or syntactic structures. These traditional methods necessitate vast labeled datasets and extensive feature engineering, which hinders the development of robust, adaptable models. In contrast, self-supervised learning (SSL) leverages unlabeled data to generate labels, mitigating the scarcity problem associated with annotated data. Let $(S, \mathfrak{m})$ denote a polynomial ring with variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$. This text considers cases where $I$ is a monomial ideal in $S$ for which the quotient ring $S/I$ is a nearly Cohen-Macaulay structure, specifically implying a condition where $\text{depth}(S/I) \geq \max \{0, d-2\}$ for $d$ representing the codimension of $I$. Machine learning offers solutions to numerous intricate data analysis challenges, though the origins of many datasets remain obscure, favoring unsupervised approaches. While quantum versions of these algorithms have been theorized, their superior performance over classical methods remains largely conjectural. This study applies the quantum variance reduction technique—focused unsupervised learning to the Bernoulli mixture model—utilizing the Hqi-2 superconducting processor. We compare results against two baseline classical algorithms and evaluate robustness against coherent noise and qubit variability by re-running experiments across different devices and with calibrated gates. Finally, we explore a quantum guided learning variant that integrates supervised data into an unsupervised framework.

We present findings from the first systematic search for planetary anomalies using the full dataset of the first field season (2018 prime fields) of the KMTNet exoplanet transit survey. By applying the well-established technique known as the planetary anomaly search, we analyzed light curves of all known transiting binaries monitored by KMTNet. Our study utilizes complete anomaly datasets from 2018 prime fields, which include KMTNet-01N, KMTNet-01S, and a combined dataset of the four southern fields (KMTNet-04N through KMTNet-04S). For the two prime fields, our work identifies 20 systems with planetary anomalies; for these systems, 13 were previously undetected. By integrating planetary anomalies to constrain the 3D orbits of such binaries, we significantly narrow orbital period ranges. Specifically, we determine orbital periods for 11 of these systems, thereby fixing their orbital inclination and deriving precise absolute masses for the companion planets.

This work introduces a differentiable, analytical approximation for shadow computation in radiometry that serves as an alternative to Monte Carlo simulation. This method integrates into the loss function formulation of inverse light field tasks, yielding a computationally efficient pipeline for solving such problems. By enabling the calculation of shadows in a way that supplants stochastic sampling, the approach facilitates integration into optimization frameworks reliant on gradient-based derivatives. We validate this method's efficacy and accuracy against various digital and physical datasets, demonstrating its superior performance in specific metrics compared to iterative solutions to the same problem.

A primary objective in urban planning is to analyze daily travel patterns within a metropolitan area to infer origin-destination demand from day-by-day observations. This study addresses the challenge by developing an entropy-maximizing estimator that models OD demand. By introducing a probabilistic framework grounded in the entropic principle, we derive estimators for both OD volumes and the corresponding attraction matrices; furthermore, we establish the consistency of these estimators regarding probabilistic convergence. Utilizing a synthetic experiment, we validate the method's efficacy, demonstrating superior performance when compared to established approaches.

We present an analytical framework to determine stable synchronization states in finite arrays of nonlinear oscillators subject to local linear coupling. This approach hinges on formulating an energy-minimization problem, where the energy function is defined by the harmonic approximation of a phase equation around its stationary points. Within this model, a key parameter represents the harmonic approximation's validity range, reflecting the magnitude of nonlinear terms in the oscillators' equations. We examine two configurations: parallel coupling, which facilitates bidirectional synchronization, and antiparallel coupling, directed toward opposite directions. Findings reveal that while parallel coupling yields a single global synchronization state—evidenced by equally phased stationary points—antiparallel coupling supports both in-phase and out-of-out-of-phase (anti-phased) synchronization. Notably, as this model parameter decreases—indicating stronger nonlinearity—the energy function develops additional local minima, resulting in richer multiplicity of stable states. We validate the analytical predictions with numerical simulations of oscillators mapped to the McKitrick equations, confirming consistency between the model and simulations in both parallel and anti-parallel coupling regimes.

This study establishes a general scheme consisting of two algorithms designed for producing uniform spanning trees. Its first component encompasses the well-known, long, uniform paths generated by both the Aldos-Broder and Wilson algorithms; its second piece involves a uniform selection from the set of trees on $V \setminus \{s\}$ that avoid a specified node $s$ (where these trees are defined without the final node and all other edges). Under this framework both algorithms are viewed as single-phase special cases where the second algorithm is executed immediately. Alternatively, by delaying the second algorithm until the first reaches a specific threshold of length equal to $n-1$ edges (the number of edges in a tree on $n$ vertices), one can formulate a biphase version of this scheme which proves to be a more efficient estimator of $UST_s$. Finally, this approach offers a theoretical basis for the previously proposed, recently-issued algorithm of Cooper and Rall (2019) and suggests an extension to multi-phase algorithms.

This study introduces the MusicTM-Dataset, which enables simultaneous modeling of sheet music, textual lyrics, and audio tracks for complete music understanding. We propose a deep multimodal architecture leveraging a symmetric design with separate but interoperable components for processing music text, lyrics, and sound to generate a shared representational space. To validate the model's efficacy, we introduce a Symmetric Music Translation task that converts standard music notation into both lyrical text and audio output. Additionally, we propose a Music Search task that locates specific instances of music text, lyrics, or audio within the musical corpus. Experimental outcomes demonstrate a strong correlation of learned latent space correlations across lyrics, music scores, and audio, while also setting new state-of-the-art benchmarks for the introduced tasks.

A primary challenge in navigating both structured and semi-structured data contexts involves effectively visualizing and analyzing textual information. This paper addresses this issue by integrating pre-trained distributed word embeddings into Ontodia—a graphical interface designed for ontology data visualization—enhanced with a new feature called "Word Cloud Clouds." Implemented via additional query queries utilizing WordNet, pre-trained FastText models, or HuggingFace's sentence-transformers embeddings, underlies simultaneous semantic word cloud generation. To further connect semantic insights to specific data points within a network, individual clusters of co-occurrent words connect to related entities through dynamic "semantic bridges," thus enabling comparative analysis between entities based on their respective semantic word cloud. To demonstrate the utility, word cloud cloud and semantic bridges were explored using a comprehensive dataset containing biographical knowledge about historical figures from the 19th and early 20th centuries, sourced from Wikidata. Word cloud cloud and semantic bridges provide an innovative semantic data exploration tool capable of uncovering meaningful connections in textual data environments.

The study provides an analytical examination of the nonlinear phase shift experienced by dark solitices within optical media whose dispersion varies with intensity. By employing a moving frame of reference frame, aligned with the nonlinear group velocity at which the solitary wave stabilizes, the investigation derives a particular equation describing this phase shift. Through the constraint that the wave's amplitude remains constant, the parameter range permitting the wave's existence is established. Furthermore, in systems where amplitude dispersion dominates, a dark solitice exhibits a nonlinearity-dependent velocity, leading to a specific relationship between the wave's amplitude and its nonlinear parameter. In contrast, within dispersion-managed systems, the amplitude of the wave is fixed, which dictates a specific value for the nonlinearity parameter.

Achieving the full potential of visual analytics (VA) systems requires active user engagement, yet effectively guiding these users remains a significant open challenge. While recent research has explored various forms of user guidance, current approaches often lack generalizability and are tightly coupled to specific VA applications. To address this, we introduce a flexible, abstracting design for user guidance that is VA-agnostic. We formalize a theoretical model of the guidance process, outline user requirements for an optimal system based on engagement, and propose a design-proposal for implementing these principles, culminating in a prototype named Lotse. Our design allows us to record and analyze user interactions, which can be reused to validate this research and support a more rigorous evaluation of the approach.

Effective heat transfer is vital for the safety of exothermic, non-catalytic reactions within porous media. In this study, we investigate reaction temperatures in a solid-fluid fixed bed using real-time magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alongside an external differential scanning calorimeter. By rapidly bringing the heated fluid into contact with the bed material, we observed that local temperatures in the fluidized zone stabilize sooner as the fluid distributes evenly around the solid particles. However, the bulk of the bed continues to rise in temperature for a prolonged duration due to thermal lag. While the fluidized region maintains a consistent arrangement of thermal profiles over time, the main bed exhibits distinct temporal variations in this structure throughout the reaction. These dynamics are accurately simulated by a convection-based model that ignores conductive heat transfer between fluid and solid surfaces, whereas traditional models incorporating both conduction and convective terms fail to capture the experimental data.

This work investigates the kinetic growth of statistical ensembles containing multiple interconnected components that self-assemble through shared elements. Such systems are prevalent in biological contexts, where entities like proteins and RNA frequently form diverse aggregates, including viruses, ribosomes, and stress granules, by leveraging a common set of parts. Our findings reveal that these systems display an effective volume exclusion principle, where potential assembly locations experience excluded volumes that are reduced compared to those in single-component models due to internal exclusion effects. While these regions remain inaccessible to formation, they are shaped by interactions among distinct components. Consequently, the positions available for assembly exhibit only partial statistical independence. However, because the effective excluded volumes fall lower than in monocompant scenarios and available assembly sites expand, the system experiences accelerated growth, leading to more robust kinetically driven phase transitions. These structural and kinetic phenomena offer significant potential to influence the assembly mechanisms of complex multicomponent entities, such as viral particles or specific stress granules.

This study examines the evolution of sunspots and magnetic fields within NOAA Active Region 11429, which displayed complex delta-shaped configurations. Analysis utilized vector magnetograms from SDO/HSI obtained every single day from June 19 to July 13, 2012, capturing the rotation of leading ($\delta$-1) and following ($\delta$-2) spots as well as bright magnetic corridors. The observed $\delta$-1 spot rotated counter-clockwise with a Period of approximately 2.66 days, while the following (B) spot and the eastern and central (C) parts of the strip followed a clockwise motion; however, the motion of the A component was not continuous due to significant fluctuations. The study identified the relative positions of these components based on their magnetic flux and categorized the active area into four specific structural stages. The research demonstrated a clear link between sunspot rotation and flare events, noting that most X-class and high-level (X-) flares resulted from the merging of magnetic fields between the A/B and A/C segments. Furthermore, the study established a correlation between Cadell numbers (a measure of sunspot complexity) and flare intensity, observing that increases in complexity preceded major flares, with new spots forming at the eastern end of the active region prior to an (X-) flare. The findings underscore that sunspot rotation and magnetic restructuring serve as critical precursors for forecasting solar flares.

This study focuses on the development of efficient numerical techniques for simulating cardiovascular mechanical behaviors, specifically addressing challenges in finite element discretization, time-step discretization, and material nonlinearities. We develop and evaluate a comparative analysis of three distinct scalable two-level and three-level finite element multilevel preconditioners designed for the two-dimensional linearization of a constitutive hyperelastic model. These preconditioners address spatial discretization and incorporate a fixed second-order central difference scheme for time-discretization. Given that these preconditioners function within full Newton iterations to solve constitutive nonlinear systems on massively parallel clusters for three-dimensional problems, a key limitation is their inability to resolve the spatially derived linear system of the constitutive equation of the two-dimensional fully implicit scheme. Consequently, we present an extended strategy that integrates all three preconditioners into a second, second-order temporal fully explicit scheme to fully resolve both spatially and temporally discrete problems. We validate the performance and efficacy of these algorithms by applying them to a three-dimensional hyperelastic constitutive model of the myocardial tissue, which includes various simulation scenarios.

Social tagging systems have established a significant presence in Web 2.0 environments, enabling users to associate descriptive metadata with resources such as web pages, emails, and documents. This capability facilitates enhanced resource discovery through improved visualization and interaction patterns, allowing for better comprehension of individual and collective user behaviors over time. A comprehensive analysis utilizing more than ten years of usage data from the automated bookmarking platform Diigo reveals four distinct patterns: (1) diverse collaboration methods employed by participants; (2) varied strategies for interest sharing, either by replicating tags on other items or appending tags to existing resources; (3) temporal variations in tag reutilization and resource sharing activities; and (2) an understanding of evolution within user interest domains. Pattern descriptions rely on an analytical framework rooted in social network analysis and the study of temporal networks.

This work introduces an all-optical approach for generating complex, structurally precise periodic acoustic metamaterials that operate with microwaves. Utilizing femtosecond pulsed lasers, this technique is based on the precise control of self-organized capillary crystal structures, specifically micro-nuggets, which self-assemble from nanoparticle suspensions under the laser beam. The resulting three-dimensional micro- and nano-porous architectures are engineered to support capillary crystal motion, providing a means to fabricate functional metamaterials at extremely high frequencies, specifically in the gigahertz (GHz) range.

This work investigates the asymptotic behavior over time, specifically approaching zero error as t approaches infinity, of global strong solutions within the 2-D FENE ribbon model that accounts for compressibility. As demonstrated in this article, as time t tends toward positive infinity, both the velocity and deformation tensor exponentially converge toward their respective equilibrium states, which vary linearly with space, at the rate $O(e^{-\lambda t})$. Here, $\lambda$ denotes the minimum of the distinct eigenvalues of both the dissipating coefficients hyped by viscosity $\nu$ and dissipation.

The concept of the Integrated Access Backhaul (IAB) was initially conceived to optimize network capacity in fixed access scenarios, yet realizing full Integrated Access Backhaul (IAB) in mobile environments remains a nascent field fraught with complications. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of the current landscape surrounding mobile IAB. It begins by recapping the IAB architecture and the 3GPP standards, then examines the complexities of radio resource management (specifically interference management, scheduling, and access/multichannel resource allocation) in mobile contexts. Furthermore, the paper explores related research on vehicular IAB, including vehicular IAB architectures and access–backhaul multiplexing strategies. Through an in-depth analysis of these issues and existing solutions, this work aims to offer researchers a thorough understanding of the field and to propose potential pathways for future investigation into mobile IAB.

This research employs Global Sensitivity Analysis (GS A) to evaluate how hyperparameters influence the effectiveness and consistency of three key algorithms in continuous optimization: differential evolution, mutation-based evolution, and simulated binary mutation. Through mu-Latin hypercube sampling and Sobol output sensitivity assessment, a primary insight emerges: algorithm performance is most significantly driven by those parameters governing exploration versus exploitation—the balance between searching new areas and refining existing promising ones. Furthermore, we observe that an ideal setting for this specific algorithm exists around an "optimal" point where hyperparameters tune the search-to-explore behavior; however, the location of this optimum shifts depending on the target function.

Current reinforcement learning (RL) methods typically treat tasks as one-off opportunities, assuming a prior existence of task-independent prior knowledge, and struggle with transferring acquired skills to subsequent problems. In contrast, this article introduces Lifelong Real-time Simulation for Lateral and Motor Skill Acquisition (L2Explorer), a new RL testbed designed to address imagination, exploration, and the heads-or-tails problem within a robotic context of picking objects from two distinct positions. This platform enables a single RL agent to learn gradually across a sequence of related challenges without initial prior knowledge or task-specific assumptions. L2Manager consists of two integrated components: (1) a dual-channel reward mechanism engineered to balance between current performance optimization and long-term capability expansion, and (2) a dynamic exploration scheduler that adjusts the rate of novel versus familiar task presentation based on real-time acquisition progress. Experimental results demonstrate that leveraging this environment effectively promotes both spatial reasoning and a robust object manipulation skill set.

Liger is the proposed name for a proposed Large Infrared Spectrometer/Imager project designed primarily to serve as a high-throughput capability for the Keck Observatory, though it could potentially adapt to other observatories. Driven by a vision of broad user engagement, the initiative integrates both human operators and virtual observers within its operational framework. To enable this diverse user base, Liger employs specialized tools, including the Virtual Instrument Configurator (VIC) and the Virtual Instrument Control (VIC), to facilitate task virtualization. Furthermore, the system relies on the Keck Common Instrument Software Suite (CISS) framework along with the AstroWorkbench environment to support diverse observers effectively. This document introduces the Liger instrument, details the architecture of its data processing system, and outlines key features of the interfaces connecting users to the instrument's control and reduction pipelines.

This work examines time-dependent, two-dimensional incompressible flows of infinite extent governed by the 2D Euler equation, focusing on how a vorticity function $\omega(t,x,y)$ evolves from a non-equilibrium state toward one that mimics a flow moving at a constant velocity $U$ in the $x$-direction (where $U \neq 0$). Specifically, it is shown that if the initial vorticity is sufficiently close in the $H^s$ norm ($s>2$) to the vorticity generated by the constant velocity shear field—given by $\gamma_U(x,y) = \omega_U(x,y) = -\frac{U}{U}(y) = -Uy$—then the subsequent dynamics preserve this proximity. More precisely, the $H^s$ distance between the time-evolving vorticity $\omega(t,\cdot)$ and $\gamma_U$ does not increase over any time interval. This result relies fundamentally on the vorticity equation $\partial_t \omega + (f_U . \nabla) \omega = 0$, where the convective term corresponds to the advection of $\gamma_U$ by the constant speed in the $x-axis. This approach extends earlier work by Masmoudi and Rousset, who addressed only convergence to zero for the Euler equations, thereby allowing their techniques to converge to a steady-state motion rather than stillness. We present the initial demonstration of pure spin states within and ocidenton-polariton condensates situated in a coupled double quantum well architecture. The observed ground state exhibits horizontal polarization along with a longitudinal density distribution featuring a central depletion, characteristic of a hard-wall Coulomb interaction regime, despite the system's low density. Leveraging an in-plane magnetic field to split the exciton-polariton energy levels, we dynamically manipulate phase and amplitude degrees of freedom to generate arbitrary linear polarization angles. This proof-of-concept paves the way for constructing a compact microscale device capable of optical polarization control, facilitating future spintronics and quantum information applications.

In early 2020, the South African Health Products Regulatory Agency (SAHPRA) maintained a real-time, centralized database tracking COVID-19 cases across the nation, which was newly constructed to integrate private sector test results from various laboratories. However, before the pandemic, limited experience existed within the data analytics community regarding the application of data integration technologies combined with machine learning algorithms for surveillance purposes. As private entities held ownership and priority control over their proprietary testing data experiences, challenges arose in accessing this information for public benefit purposes without legal frameworks established at that time facilitating data sharing initiatives voluntarily. A multidisciplinary team of data analysts and researchers worked collaboratively to develop accessible visualization systems providing timely updates to the general population through mobile applications and internet-based dashboards. By analyzing historical patterns of virus transmission alongside current diagnostic capabilities, researchers projected potential hotspots of infection while identifying strategic locations for additional facility deployment. Furthermore, researchers evaluated operational bottlenecks within existing workflows and identified specific processes requiring streamlining to enhance testing throughput. Recognizing that diagnostic results often arrived with notable delays, researchers proposed implementing automated data pipelines capable of ingesting, transforming, and moving information rapidly between systems for immediate processing. By leveraging established data contracts ensuring consistent communication protocols, researchers established reliable transfer mechanisms ensuring seamless exchange of standardized information structures. Finally, researchers proposed establishing a unified data contract framework governing the exchange processes between government agencies and private sector partners to establish formal protocols for collaborative data interoperability efforts.

Glaucoma and Diabetic Retinopathy are among the leading global causes of irreversible blindness. While both conditions manifest distinct retinal and optic nerve characteristics, they often coexist; therefore, research into their relationships is vital for improving clinical care and AI-driven diagnostics. This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to detect glaucoma and manage DR by leveraging fused multimodal data from fundus photos and OCT scans. The architecture utilizes separate encoder branches to extract features from different modalities, which are then combined into a shared decoder for joint learning. Although standard fusion strategies focus on early or late integration, the proposed system implements full fusion across the entire processing pipeline. Experiments utilizing the DRORIS dataset demonstrated superior performance in classifying both glaucoma and Diabetic Retinopathy when the model incorporated OCT information. Specifically, the OA-ResNet34 model with fused multimodal data achieved Glaucoma and Diabetic Retinopathy accuracy scores of 92.8% and 96.8%, respectively.

The ongoing global pandemic caused by SARS-CoV-2 has resulted in widespread ICU admissions, placing a severe strain on ICU resources and necessitating automated monitoring systems to detect ICU cases of COVID-19. Since Chest X-rays are the primary diagnostic method for identifying the virus, this study examines data from Chest X-rays to determine which features can reliably predict ICU admissions, with findings indicating that ICU status is associated with specific regions in the X-ray images. While the image processing workflow involved standardizing patient data, normalizing pixel values, and segmenting lung fields to isolate areas of interest, this approach is currently restricted to Brazilian X-rays, emphasizing the requirement for future datasets to be geographically diversified.

To uncover user intent from dialogue, we introduce an innovative approach that leverages the user's intent history to fine-tune BERT with contrastive learning. Our framework consists of two phases. During the first, we utilize a pre-training task that (a) predicts the current intent based on the entire conversation and (b) performs mutual information maximization to fuse information from user utterances with issue keywords. Consequently, the embeddings develop a stronger association between dialogue context and intent. In the second phase, we execute a contrastive learning technique to optimize the loss function so that samples sharing the same intent exhibit proximity in embedding space, whereas dissimilar samples are pushed apart. This enables simple and efficient intent classification via minimum distance calculation. Furthermore, we enhance this training with two novel data augmentation strategies: extracting entities and keywords from web search results to construct contrastive pairs, and utilizing permuted conversation segments to generate negative samples. Empirical assessments across two public datasets and private ones confirm that this method attains top-tier performance.

The Hunt–Kincaid absorption model, introduced in 1982 and re-examined in 1987, serves as a highly effective framework for investigating wave absorption across various media. This study analyzes wave propagation characteristics within the hybrid framework provided by the ABS H2 equation, analyzing solutions for impulse, sinusoidal waves, and observing the medium's impact. Furthermore, energy analyses of the wave groups provide detailed insights into the mechanisms of wave absorption.

Visual relationship detection aims to identify semantic interactions between objects in an image; however, generating spurious relationships remains a primary obstacle to the widespread adoption of this technology. This study investigates the origins of such false positives by analyzing semantic, visual, and syntactic characteristics across positive and negative sample pairs. Furthermore, we propose a novel framework termed Verbal Guidance (VG) to mitigate these errors. VG leverages pre-trained multilingual large language models to generate descriptive narratives for image instances. By presenting these generated descriptions to a visual relation detector, VG effectively grounds the process in semantics and substantially lowers the rate of false positive detections. Empirical evaluations conducted on six relevant datasets confirm the efficacy of VG, demonstrating significant performance improvements over current state-of-the-art methods specifically regarding false positive reduction.

We introduce an operator-dependent measure termed Quantum Correlation Price (OQCP) for weak measurements. Since weak measurements yield only minimal information, their efficiency in generating quantum correlations is naturally constrained, a limitation that the QCP captures. Conversely, for unitary evolution, we propose the Quantum Correlation Cost-QCP (QCPCd), a metric reflecting the extensive correlation production capability, a phenomenon opposite to that of weak measurements. We establish the optimality of both the QCP and QCPCd within frameworks analyzing measurement precision and correlation evolution. Furthermore, we investigate non-equilibrium thermodynamic cycles operating on thermal baths, utilizing weak and unitary operations to highlight the distinct behaviors of these corresponding operators when the initial state exhibits classical correlations. Finally, we examine the trade-off between information and thermodynamic work, examining how weak and unitary operations process knowledge and work extraction capabilities.

Socially driven decision-making often depends on relationship types that vary continuously rather than falling into fixed categories. To visualize this spectrum, we suggest mapping the duration an agent spends near another to specific relational categories, where the spectral attributes drive this mapping. Leveraging this proposal, we have created an initial framework capable of generating social relationship diagrams directly from unsupervised video footage. First, relationships are represented as complete graph edges weighted by the speaker-listener distance. Next, these weights are projected using eigenvalues and eigenvectors onto a unit interval, where specific endpoints represent socially intimate and isolated states. Finally, a segment of the unit interval is assigned to each edge to capture intermediate relational phases. We have developed a fully convolutional neural network to perform this unit-interval mapping end-to-end. This network receives an image patch as input and outputs the corresponding segments on the unit interval. Additionally, we proposed a segmentation mechanism to isolate edges situated near intimate or isolated representations. Experiments on synthesized data produced from a multi-agent simulation validate our suggestions.

However, both standard CNNs and existing CNN-derived architectures like CPNs are limited by their fixed convolution kernels, which hinder their ability to capture visual features with a dynamic kernel. In response, this paper introduces Dynamic Graph Communication Passing Networks (DGCPN), designed to overcome these deficiencies by enabling the dynamic discovery of non-local information using an adaptable kernel. Specifically, DGCPN establishes a unified framework where DG kernels evolve dynamically based on detected features. Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) is vital for various multimedia and telecommunications applications. While many methods exist, the most efficient hardware implementation typically involves a systolic multiplier arrangement that maximizes multiplications ($\times2$) and minimizes both the count of necessary multipliers and the operational delay. Achieving optimal logic complexity, operation latency, and multiple constant coefficients simultaneously remains difficult. This study introduces an innovative algorithm designed to minimize multiplications for any given MCM vector. The core strategy relies on sorting the MCM factors in ascending order before applying the algorithm. Complexity metrics are then estimated using a newly derived closed-form expression. The methodology is both versatile and universal, applicable to any MCM operation. Validation through an examination of 1,000 randomly selected MCM instances confirms the findings and illustrates the significant advantages of the new approach compared to existing solutions in reduced hardware cost for identifying the minimal multiplication count.

Deep learning's recent success is largely rooted in innovative ideas for defining neural network architectures, which have recently begun gaining traction within quantum machine learning as well. In this context, quantum neural architectures utilize features like superposition and high expressivity to drive performance. This review examines the latest developments in quantum neural architectures, highlighting both the promising potential and the significant implementation hurdles. It concludes by proposing future pathways to advance this field, aiming to establish solid foundations for robust quantum-based machine learning algorithms capable of securing advantages over classical methods in specific tasks, particularly through the use of mid-circuit measurements in the design process.

We analyze the linearized equations governing both causal and acausal phases within a viscous relativistic fluid framework. Our investigation demonstrates a critical divergence between the viscous drag term, which slightly modifies the amplitude decay rate of the modes but leaves their dispersion relations unchanged versus the viscous heat flux, which significantly alters both amplitude decay rates and the modal dispersion characteristics. This study investigates the potential contribution of ultrahigh- to very-high-energy (UHE/VHE) galactic radio particles generated by Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) evaporating today, specifically those with a mass around $10^{15}$ g. The research demonstrates that such an historical population of evaporating PBHs could significantly influence the observed fluxes of UHE neutrinos detected by IceCube and of UHE gamma rays observed by HAWC. This paper introduces the Virtual Safeguard Platform, a novel architecture designed for secure remote CPU simulation. It achieves precise computation confidentiality by combining homomorphically encrypted microcode, data, and instruction sets with a series of specialized hardware units. These components rely on Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), specifically the BFV scheme and its Lattice-based variant, TLint. To manage performance bottlenecks inherent to TDL and Tlnt operations, we developed a VLSI-friendly encoding scheme and applied arithmetical decompositions. Our architecture utilizes a five-stage pipeline processor capable of executing a custom set of FHE-enabled arithmetic, bitwise, and comparison operators. Our evaluation demonstrates a 4.4x acceleration over prior art, reducing execution time for the TDL arithmetic bitarder to 24.1 ms and the Time complexity bitader to 18.7 ms. Furthermore, we achieved a 14.4x reduction in silicon area relative to earlier platforms, validating our design's potential for practical, privacy-preserving processing.

Valued Constraint Optimization Problems (VALUED CSPs), which encompass diverse optimization contexts like those involving weighted model counting, have been studied extensively since their formalization. Pessard et al. demonstrated that the complexity of these valued problems relative to instances depends entirely on their underlying valued constraints. Building on this, we analyze the complexity valued solutions across sparsely populated instances and establish that generic sparsification strategies allow for the construction of a PTAS. This result is supported by an algorithm with polynomial in instance size that has a degradation factor proportional to the number of distinct valued constraints, which counts as part of problem parameters. We further show that the graph density of instances—relative to graph structures formed by valued constraints—is a suitable parameter for approximation solutions in cases where instances are not sparse.

Pretrained language models offer significant capabilities across various tasks, largely due to their extensive knowledge base; their ability to capture semantic and syntactical structures makes them particularly valuable for understanding human reasoning mechanisms. While many existing approaches investigate these internal representations using visualization techniques, they often fall short in providing a comprehensive account of the models' cognitive processes. To address this, we introduce Unsupervised and Few-shot reasoning analysis, a novel strategy that facilitates insight without the need for task-specific labeled datasets. Our experiments reveal that these internal layers execute reordering operations to resolve ambiguities, execute computations to determine set membership, and execute pattern matching to identify entity relations, all while maintaining interpretability. Furthermore, we uncovered recurring structures across different models indicative of conceptual reasoning strategies. In conclusion, our findings underscore the necessity of employing unsupervised analysis methods to deepen the investigation into how these advanced systems process and comprehend language.

This study explores a framework for hyperspectral photograph analysis. Unlike conventional images with three color channels, hyperspectral photographs consist of multiple spectral bands, offering the ability to distinguish various object types with granular precision. While their superior classification potential remains largely untapped in current segmentation research, this study addresses that gap. We leverage both high-order dependencies across spectral dimensions and spatial correlations between adjacent pixels to enhance performance. On the challenging Drive-Scene dataset, which features complex structures like vehicles and roads, our proposed model surpasses SOTA methods, achieving gains of up to 10.5% over leading techniques.

The observed spin-up of K2-18b's atmosphere is puzzling because the planet's equilibrium tidal response cannot account for the observed momentum. We investigate the evolution of a planetary system where K2-18b might have devoured a super-Earth companion, utilizing either a high eccentricity tidal model or planet-planet interactions to address this discrepancy. Our simulations confirm that consuming an estimated $M_p \approx 7 M_\oplus$ of material during a highly eccentric merger can suffice to reach the necessary angular momentum. Additionally, interactions between two planets with initial masses of $M_p \approx 5 M_\oplus$ and $M_p \approx 10 M_\oplus$ can also replicate these observations. While eccentricity decay offers the most consistent explanation, our results also show that adjacent planets can effectively migrate inward together to match these conditions. Ultimately, this scenario suggests K2-18b retains a massive core ($M_p \gtrsim 5-10 M_\oplus$) driving its observed spin rate, which could potentially reveal similar signatures for other planets exhibiting rapid rotation.

In the RAM model with multiplication, executing any of the standard arithmetic operations takes constant time. By contrast, when the RAM is equipped only with additive operations within the natural numbers, it remains uncertain whether multiplication can occur in constant time; even this basic possibility has not been resolved. A critical initial step toward resolving such hardness is identifying other operations that execute efficiently relative to constant time. This paper demonstrates that within both integers and nonnegative rationals within $\mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}$, logarithmic power functions become constant-time operations under addition-only constraints given an upper bound on inputs. This finding suggests that multiplication can be computed via logarithmic duality using only logarithmic transformations—specifically exp and power—which are now constant time on a machine with just additive capabilities to handle large integers.
Additionally, we show constant time feasibility on an machine restricted only with logarithmic power functions $f(x)=x^f$ for integers $f \ge 1$.
This suggests that even with logarithmic power functions we have enough to multiply two large integers in constant time on an RAM machine restricted only with logarithmic power functions.

Session-based recommendation aims to predict the next item by modeling user sessions, which typically involve sequences of interacted items, as this approach offers significant privacy advantages by eliminating the need for user profiles, which only contemporary, well-structured systems can benefit from. Most current approaches rely on supervised labeling, which necessitates extensive storage space for historical interactions and generates a deluge of false labels due to difficulties in accurately defining ground truth. In contrast, this paper introduces a self-supervised learning method designed to generate supplementary, session-specific training data by extracting supplementary patterns from items within each session, which enables more effective model training and improves overall recommendation systems by generating more data for training without the need to label existing data. This method implements graph-based neural networks integrated into joint graph embeddings alongside cooperative learning to generate consistent, session-based recommendations. Experiments conducted on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of next-item prediction.

This paper introduces new classes of LCD codes when viewed through the lens of group theory, specifically defining and characterizing group LCD codes. We establish detailed links between group ring group LCD codes and those that are simply LCD. Characterizing properties for group ring group LCD codes are derived using the idempotents of the ring $R$. Finally, we characterize group ring group reversible and non-reversible self-dual codes within $C_{2n}$. As concrete applications of this new theory we provide examples of explicit group ring group reversible and non-reversible self-dual codes in $C_{\,n}$. Groups $G$ include both cyclic ones defined on $Z_p^*$ where $p$ is a prime, as well as dihedral, alternating, and symmetric groups defined on $Z_{p+1}^f$, all within the context of these coding theories applications.

We establish a set of graph homomorphisms capable of deformingly modifying lattice Feynman integrands defined on projective d-dimensional invariant differential shapes. As d increases beyond 2, these shapes evolve from orientable surfaces into general topological complexes characterized by non-zero homologies and diversities of complexes that we now construct via graph homomorphisms. Along with introducing a set of rules that deformingly modify integrands based on graph features like symmetry, loop number, and dimension, we will demonstrate a set universal rules for evaluating integrands on all complexes generated.

Although object categories are often considered the primary source of information in vision, researchers recognize that various object properties also possess functional significance. For instance, an object's shape may dictate manual handling methods, while its material may influence decision-making regarding consumption, indicating that active visual learning must sometimes prioritize traits orthogonal to categorical identity. Yet, understanding whether both trait and categorical information can coexist during neural representation is still unclear, especially given that focusing solely on one might preclude the other due to competition, suggesting that active visual systems require mechanisms to encode them independently. Addressing this gap, the current work evaluates the capability of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) in simultaneously learning categorical trait traits through a specialized training protocol. We observe that while standard classification RNNs implicitly encode the dataset's background gradients, our new RNN model trained using category-orthogonal object images successfully acquires traits independent of category. Furthermore, analyzing layer-specific intermediate states reveals that this unique training approach distributes both categorical trait information across distinct, segregated regions, thereby supporting their non-competitive, simultaneous encoding. These findings demonstrate that artificial RNN networks can be guided to simultaneously master object categories and independent traits, providing a potential pathway toward artificial visual systems capable of multifaceted property recognition essential for active visual perception and manipulation tasks.

This study examines non-Hermitian topology in one-dimensional chains of resonators, a system characterized by anti-hermitian couplings that lead to eigenstates' delocalization once a point-gap is breached. The analysis spans scenarios with uniform and position-dependent (quasi-periodic) potentials. While the former system supports a non-trivial point-gap topological index, systems exhibiting a non-trivial index manifest in exceptional ring structures in their energy spectra. The research reveals that interactions among modes trigger intermodal energy exchange when the point gap reduces to zero at an exceptional point, causing the collapse of this topological invariant. The same holds for higher winding numbers in regimes allowing multi-winding topologies. The findings are validated analytically using the Husimi index and numerically via the Slater-Pokorny invariant, and they are corroborated by simulations of light propagation within the test structure, which align perfectly with analytical and numerical results.

This research introduces designs for polyphase Golay complementary arrays (GCAs), extending the recently discovered binary GCA pattern. We propose three distinct construction methods: the first method generalizes the binary GCA design introduced in literature. Our second and third methods, however, are entirely new approaches for generating GCA patterns involving more than two phases.

This study examines the on-shell and off-shell production of the Higgs boson via vector boson fusion in the final state containing four leptons, utilizing CMS dataset collected at the LHC during Run 2 (2016-2018), which integrates 137 fb$^{-1}$ of luminosity. Detecting changes between co-registered multispectral datasets is critical across various sectors like urban planning, agriculture, and defense, particularly within the formative stage involving the comparison of two spectral images to uncover discrepancies. Specifically, this approach yields the multiplicity of each irreducible character in the regular representation. Internal symmetries are now recognized as a fundamental component of the standard model, which accounts for the vast majority of known phenomena in particle physics. Digital vector maps represent linear geographic features using mathematical primitives like lines and curves; however, when these elements join or terminate near the edges of map tiles, they often exhibit visual flaws such as jaggedness or unwanted brightness variations caused by screen pixel discretization. To remediate this, a spatial anti-aliasing approach is proposed that generates an effective blur layer over specific join and end zones. This process utilizes both straight line segments and cubic Bezier curves to compute a blended background color based on neighbor areas. Specifically for end points, distances to adjacent pixels are calculated via ray casting toward curve or line edges, or alternatively, by employing a pre-calculated 2D distance field. Finally, the resulting layer is composed by applying this distance-based alpha mask as a blend mask to the calculated background color.

This study examines how new social norms regarding climate change originate and spread across different societal domains such as politics, economics, and ethics. This study introduces a virtual soft-solid interaction simulator utilizing Hamiltonian mechanics, which enables real-time, model-based control of multi-fingered grippers by extending recently developed theories on operator theory applied to nonlinear dynamical systems. Specifically, the Koopman approach transforms a nonlinear system into a linear one observables, creating a formal link between the original system and its normalized counterpart. Leveraging this mechanism, we transfer learning capabilities from a reference system to a target system, effectively bridging the simulation-reality divide for training purposes. Graphical models offer a unified framework for describing probabilistic relationships among variables, where efficient inference relies on their inherent exact correlations to optimization tasks. This paper introduces a novel generalization of gradient descent, termed the "organic gradient descent," utilizing weighted combinations of dual variables within these models. We establish that this method succeeds in optimizing both convex and non-convolic objectives, reduces computational complexity compared to traditional gradient approaches by eliminating dual variable evaluation during updates, and enables direct generation of an optimal solution path. These properties facilitate accelerated inference in large-scale, high-dimensional, and sparse settings.
